subject: alt text for images and svg

messages.subject: alt text for images and svg
parts:
Hi All,

I have two questions mostly related to knitr and the web. I work on a
relatively large website (http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/), but do not
actually have much background in web design. I have been
transitioning the R pages to use knitr which has been fantastic. Now
we are making some other transitions to the website and I am
considering a couple other changes but was hoping for some feedback.

1) So far I haved used the default PNG format for images. I am
thinking of moving to use SVG because leaving the graphics in a vector
format seems more flexible to me in terms of quality, size, etc. Is
there a reason _not_ to do this?

2) For accessibility purposes, I want to start adding alt text to
images. I think this can be done with the additional options chunk
argument. However, I cannot see if there is a way to do it if tehre
are multiple images in one chunk. Any ideas? Worst case, I can just
only include one image per chunk.

Thanks!

Josh


--
Joshua Wiley

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] alt text for images and svg
parts:
1. I have no idea about the support in IE, and that is the only
possible reason that SVG may not be preferable in my opinion (I guess
IE8-9 must be good enough now); in terms of quality, I do not see a
big difference. One other reason that SVG may not be a good idea is
the file size; with a large number of graphical elements, the SVG file
can be huge.

2. fig.cap = c('a', 'vector', 'of', 'figure', 'captions') (at least
with the latest version of knitr)

Regards,
Yihui
